text:
maria: Heads-up — scheduling a serial apply for the release window tonight 22:00-23:00 UTC. This touches VPC routing + a small IAM role change. Reserving slot #3 in the apply queue.
kevin: slot 3 noted. Is the IAM change a new trust policy or just a policy tweak?
maria: trust policy update — we're swapping trust from `dev-ci` -> `release-runner` for the service account. Plan shows only the AssumeRole block changing.
deploy-bot: queued apply #3: terraform plan completed, awaiting apply window. ETA slot start 22:20 UTC. State lock will be taken when apply starts.
infra-oncall: reminder — keep state lock under 10m if possible. If apply runs longer, we should escalate and decide whether to split network vs iam.
sarah: Agree. Suggest we run network module first, then IAM as a follow-up canary. If network is fine, we proceed with IAM in same window but separate apply.
maria: plan sounds good. I'll pin provider and module versions before apply: `versions.tf` locked to `terraform 1.5.9` and aws provider `~> 4.50`.
dylan: Can we prepare a rollback snippet in case the trust change breaks downstream CI? Want a quick revert command.
sarah: Copy/paste for rollback: ```bash
# revert trust back to dev-ci
git checkout -b rollback/iam-trust
# restore previous commit of iam-module
git revert <commit-sha>
# apply only iam module
terraform apply -target=module.iam -auto-approve
```
kevin: Also add a step to re-grant the old role in IAM console if terraform fails to reapply. Manual fallback note in release notes.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: slot #3 starting apply now. Taking remote state lock. Logs: `apply started by maria`
infra-oncall: If we see `Error: precondition failed` from the state backend, cancel and retry after 30s. If persists, open an incident channel.
maria: Running apply for `module.network` first: `terraform apply -target=module.network -auto-approve` — watching for route table replacement.
dylan: If route table replacement happens, what is expected downtime?
maria: Should be sub-10s thanks to target replacement and healthy routes. Will announce if we need to drain hosts.
sarah: After network apply completes, I'll run a dry-run for the IAM apply and test assume-role with a short-lived session: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/release-runner --duration-seconds 900`
kevin: Marking this in the release notes: "IAM trust migration — rollback plan included, manual console fallback documented."
maria: Network apply complete. No route replacements. Proceeding to IAM now.
deploy-bot: apply finished for slot #3: success. State lock released.
infra-oncall: Post-apply checks: confirm CloudWatch alarms healthy, and verify no increase in denied AssumeRole logs for 15m.
sarah: STS assume-role test succeeded. I see no denied logs.
dylan: Adding final note to release changelog: `2026-03-20: VPC routing apply + IAM trust migration; canaries green; rollback steps recorded.` :tada:
maria: Thanks team. Closing the slot and updating the release channel with the PR link and rollback snippet.
kevin: Great job — filing a brief postmortem checklist in case we want to automate the rollback path next time.
maria: Agree — follow-up ticket to add a canary test in CI around AssumeRole.
deploy-bot: This thread archived by deploy-bot.
